classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the cut pyramid as two square faces and four congruent trapeziums, recognise 3.5 cm as the trapezium height, and combine their areas.

content.prompt:
The solid opposite is called a frustum. It is the portion of a square pyramid that remains after the upper part has been cut off by a plane parallel to its base.
What is the surface area of the frustum? Answer correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded square-pyramid frustum with explicit planar faces and viewing direction. Single ticks identify the four equal bottom edges; double ticks identify the four equal top edges. The labelled 3.5 cm segment is the front trapezium face height, with a right-angle marker at its upper endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Bottom square side 4 cm; top square side 2 cm; trapezium face height 3.5 cm. The perpendicular solid height used only to construct the model is sqrt(3.5^2-1^2)=sqrt(11.25) cm and is not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no surface areas are supplied.

answer.worked:
Top square: $2^2=4\ \mathrm{cm}^2$.

Bottom square: $4^2=16\ \mathrm{cm}^2$.

The $3.5\ \mathrm{cm}$ measurement is the height of each trapezium face.

$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{four trapeziums}}&=4\left(\frac{(2+4)\times3.5}{2}\right)\\&=42\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=4+16+42\\&=62.0\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{aligned}$$
